_doc: The role registry: one entry per role, the single source of its mode, model, effort, budget, value metric and agent permissions. Edit with `python -I -X utf8 tools/work/roles.py set <role> key=value ...` (it regenerates); `roles.py gen` writes .opencode/agents/<role>.md (its body: `body_common`, then the role's `body` or `helper_block`), tools/work/helper.md (from `helper_block`) and the model line of each listed command; `roles.py check` (tools/work/tests/test_role_registry.py) fails on any drift. A role is in this checkout when one of its `briefs` is (none listed: always); gen and check skip the rest. `model`: the deploy fills it from your answers (`effort`, when set, is added as `#<effort>`). Budgets: $ at list prices (subscription models too); the defaults are the source project's history to 2026-11-27, so set your own after a week (`roles.py show`). `budget_mode` `warn` (until `warn_until`, when set): `may` prints and logs an overspend but exits 0 for budget; `block` exits 1. Spend counts this project's sessions only (`projects`, role_data.project_of). `briefs`: also the files whose required commands every agent must allow (test). `git_deny` holds every banned git subcommand. Value: metrics role-telemetry.py computes; `good` is the direction that counts as good; a metric with too little data rates `unknown`. `git_deny` verbs expand to `*git <v> *`, `*git <v>`, `*git -C * <v> *` and `*git -C * <v>`; `shell_allow` makes the shell an allowlist (deny `*` first).

protect._doc: Only these roles may change what drives the roles: the agent files, the commands, the registry.

projects._doc: Which project a session is (role_data.project_of), in order: `exclude` by title (an explicit line beats every heuristic: the owner's overrule goes here); `folder` (default: this checkout's main tree name, with or without `-wt`); the parent's project; a brief naming `word` (default: the main tree's folder name) once `preamble` (a spawn line naming the main tree's .work) is cut out; else `other`. Budgets and `may` count `this` only.

helper_block: `helper` is a session on the small model (`{{M_HELPER}}`) that only reads. Hand it a read when the reading is big and the answer small, and don't be shy about it: it is the cheap way to keep your own context small.
- **Use it for:** multi-file reads or summaries; "find where X is used" sweeps; log triage (what failed first); gathering the inventory for `kmap list`.
- **Not for:** judgment calls, edits, or anything whose answer you would re-check line by line anyway.

- **How:** the subagent tool, agent `helper`, with a brief that stands alone: the question, the paths, the answer's form (at most 20 lines, a `file:line` per claim, "not found" allowed only after a search that ran; a refused call is reported as refused). Read the lines it points at before you build on them.

Per 100k tokens read (list prices of 2026-11-27, `tools/work/model-prices.json`): a small model (Haiku 5.5) $0.01 input ($0.0125 into its cache); a top model (Opus 5.5) $0.50 into its cache, then $0.02 on every later request it stays in your context (Fable 5.2: $1.00, then $0.02).
1. "Which of these 30 files use `parseConfig`, with file:line?" (~120k tokens): helper ~$0.02 in all; read by an Opus builder, $0.60 now plus ~$0.024 a request, ~$3 over its next 100 requests.
2. "What failed first in this gate log?" (~100k tokens): helper ~$0.015; read by Opus, $0.50 plus $0.02 a request, ~$2.50 over 100 requests.
body_common: **A refused call is not an answer.** When a tool call is refused (`Permission denied`) or fails, say so in your answer: never report "not found", "none" or "no match" from it. Try the grep or read tool instead (a search for a word your shell rules refuse, such as `node` or `docker`, goes through the grep tool), or ask the session that sent you.
common_deny: nothing here needs a skill (the list is ~4.9k tokens a request, measured)
Code Mode; with it off its tools turn direct, so those go too
briefs: never the Playwright MCP browser tools
lookups are git grep, tools/work/map.py and tools/kmap/kmap.py
outside facts come from a role with websearch
unattended: the base policy asks here, and nobody answers a spawned session
shell_note: Measured live (opencode 2.4.1, PowerShell, 2026-11-28): opencode checks each subcommand of a chain (`|`, `;`, `&&`) alone (`git log | Select-String` was refused under a `git log` allowlist). A cmdlet, alias or script command's resource starts with the command (`npm ci *`, `Set-Content *`, `del *`, `python* -c *` matched); an `.exe` such as git or rg has text before it (`git push *` and `rg *` did not match, `* git push *` and `* rg *` did). So a word in `word_deny`/`shell_allow` expands to `<w> *`, `<w>`, `* <w> *`, `* <w>` (a whole word: `del` no longer hits `storeModel`; it still refuses an argument that is the bare word, e.g. `rg -n del`), a verb in `git_deny`/`git_allow` to those forms of `git <v>` and `git -C <path> <v>`; `shell_deny` keeps operators only.

product.when: the owner's feedback or tasks to groom (xhigh for a first plan)

agent.subagent_why: PLANNING.md: pre-groomers, the gate, the plan review, helpers
agent.edit_why: the product lead never touches code
agent.description: The product lead (was: planner) by docs/PLANNING.md: specs and new rows; never code

architect.when: each planning pass's gate (heavy rows: How to build; light: Fit); sweeps at a clean stage (#xhigh); a design call

agent.edit_why: the architect never writes feature code
agent.description: The architect (was: CTO) by docs/workflow/architect.md: How to build, Fit, sweeps, refactor rows; never feature code

plan-review.when: once per planning pass that makes a spec ready, fresh, after the architect's gate

agent.edit_why: plan-review.md: never edit specs, rows or code
agent.description: Reviews one planning pass by docs/workflow/plan-review.md, fresh per pass; findings only
agent.git_why: plan-review.md: findings only, never a commit of its own

pregroomer.when: one per heavy task, the owner's pick in the product lead's one question per pass

agent.description: Pre-grooms one task for the product lead by docs/workflow/pregroomer.md

librarian.when: a clean stage after the architect, or a doc over its budget

agent.edit_why: librarian.md: never code, tests, scripts or config
agent.description: Keeps the docs true and short by docs/workflow/librarian.md; docs only

helper.when: a read, a lookup or a summary for another session (/ask)

agent.description: A read, a lookup or a summary for another session (/ask); reads only
shell_deny: a helper only reads: no redirect
body: You answer one read-only question for another session (/ask): read what it names, then answer in at most 20 lines with a `file:line` per claim. "Not found" is an answer only after a search that ran; a refused or failed call is reported as refused. Search for a word your shell rules refuse (`node`, `docker`, `cmd`, `ssh`, `sh` ...) with the grep tool. You change nothing.
word_deny: a helper only reads: no write, move or other tool (each subcommand of a chain is checked alone)

coordinator.when: the owner's entry point; runs `roles.py may <role>` before every spawn

agent.why: the owner's own session, on the model they pick; it needs every tool

builder.when: a ready row: a lane the coordinator spawns

agent.description: A builder lane: one batch at a time in its own worktree, by docs/workflow/lane-brief.md, unattended
agent.subagent_why: lane-brief: no subagents of your own but helper
agent.git_why: lane-brief: never pull, push, change git config or check out main; never git clean -x

reviewer.when: a lane's light-GREEN line or READY: one fresh reviewer per round

agent.description: Reviews one batch by docs/workflow/reviewer-brief.md, fresh per review
agent.git_why: reviewer-brief: never push; a review never resets or removes a worktree

integrator.when: READY branches to merge; a model only on a conflict, NEW-RED, FAIL or ERROR twice

agent.description: Merges READY branches into local main by docs/workflow/integrator-brief.md
agent.git_why: integrator-brief: the integrator never removes a worktree
